Apple's new Mac Mini M6 might be the device that quietly ends the "pay monthly for AI" era — and I tested it to find out if that's actually true.

I ran real local AI workloads on the M6 to check tokens/sec, memory ceiling, and where it falls short compared to a Strix Halo mini PC and an Nvidia DGX Spark. This isn't a spec-sheet comparison — it's hands-on numbers from my own setup, the same way I test every tool on this channel.

What you'll see in this video:
- Real tokens/sec benchmarks running local LLMs on Mac Mini M6
- Where the unified memory ceiling actually breaks down under heavier models
- Mac Mini M6 vs Strix Halo vs Nvidia DGX Spark — honest side-by-side
- Why "no more AI subscriptions" is true for some workflows and false for others
- Mark Gurman's M7 rumor and what it means if you're deciding whether to buy now or wait
